sections_read: A velocity circle with controlled turns
claim_as_stated: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface, including disconnected and nonorientable surfaces, admits a C-infinity isometric immersion into Euclidean four-space; self-intersections are allowed and Gaussian curvature is unrestricted.
proof_architecture: Prepare a strictly short spherical immersion lambda I_P with the global negative radial normal. Modify it at the finite set of boundary crossings so the second fundamental form in S^3 vanishes there, with C^2 bounds independent of the number and separation of points.

Decompose the positive deficit into finitely many rank-one tensors a_j^2 dx_j^2. Perturb disk boundaries and phases using transversality, and use sufficiently many finite cycles so every prescribed intermediate metric has the positive transverse phase-Hessian condition needed for its next addition.

For each primitive addition use a periodic velocity circle in span(G_y,G_yy)^perp with prescribed mean, exact leading metric, and controlled turns. Orthogonality to G_yy removes the first transverse metric error; a finite triangular periodic expansion removes nonzero modes to a prescribed finite order.

Construct small oscillatory increments on good phases and all their doubles and pairwise sums/differences. Finite parametrix iterations and finite quadratic-mean substitutions give arbitrary finite accuracy; for a polynomial higher-jet perturbation the exponent p=E+6 is fixed independently of that accuracy.

Use smoothing of inputs only, add increments to the unsmoothed current map, and exploit the exact quadratic error identity so high derivatives enter linearly. Hold each derivative block until its next controlled norm is bounded, then increase the block; summable tails converge in every C^m norm to the exact metric with small C^2 displacement.

Use the exact Gauss equation plus the realized yy,xy and scaled xx derivatives to preserve nonvanishing, non-antipodality and both ordered crossing invariants. Glue a preferred normal through the exterior collar and iterate the finite primitive list to reach g exactly.

claim_as_stated: For arbitrary smooth admissible one-species three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell data with f_0 nonnegative and compactly supported in phase space, E_0,B_0 in C_b-infinity intersect L^2, and both divergence constraints, there is a unique global classical solution, smooth on every finite interval with compact phase-space support. No size or symmetry restrictions are imposed.
proof_architecture: Transport f along the phase-volume-preserving characteristic flow, conserve total energy, and derive the backward-cone energy flux budget. Obtain exact retarded field kernels and their initial-cone boundary terms by changing retarded phase points to initial source labels.

Assume the signed momentum-increment bootstrap |Delta V_X| <= MP sqrt(I)+AI P^2 log(2+P)/w. Decompose sources by momentum, distance, source/receiver/cone angles; use three exact changes of variables to estimate occupation. Build one joint energy budget E_(p,phi) independent of source angle and distance.
Combine density and occupation near/far estimates, retaining shared field and particle budgets under summation. Direct absolute-force control loses sqrt(w) only in the narrow source-angle region.

In that region combine transport and source-acceleration kernels before taking norms. An exact source-trajectory integration by parts produces a total derivative, a less singular geometric residual and a receiver-acceleration coefficient, while explicitly keeping cutoff, time-ramp, projector and initial-cone terms.

First use signed cancellation and baseline occupation to bound direction changes; only afterward derive improved occupation in a high-momentum intermediate-angle window. Select bins whose direct cost exceeds a summable weight. An unsafe selected receiver coefficient forces exact rational exponent inequalities into that window, where improved occupation contradicts them; the summed coefficient w^(-1/2) cancels the absolute-force loss.

Restore endpoint ramps with signed increments and close the bootstrap by a strict improvement, choosing eta, M, A and then P_0. Momentum-doubling times have a divergent harmonic lower bound, excluding finite-time blow-up. Supply local uniqueness, smooth persistence and finite-horizon field modification to invoke bounded-momentum continuation for the stated finite-energy initial class.

claim_as_stated: For every elliptic curve E/Q with full q-power Selmer corank zero or one at some prime q, the analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks equal that corank, Sha is finite, and the full BSD leading-term formula holds with all prime factors and no extra reduction, torsion, isogeny, CM or residual-representation hypotheses.
proof_architecture: Read sections 01-02: use the companion unrestricted low-corank converse for rank and whole-Sha finiteness, and a distinct companion two-primary formula for positive rationality and the valuation at 2. Define the odd-prime discrepancy X_p(E); choose two compatible imaginary quadratic fields by the stated twist-density input and derive a full-index real discrepancy identity before valuations.

Read section 03: construct bounded finite free cochain models with maps, cup products, duality, traces and homotopies marked; retain torsion and derived base change. Establish determinant-volume conventions, line/square switches, exact strict-versus-finite volume comparisons, Kummer Haar factors, and high-character integral division.

Read section 04: use tame variables and Frobenius evaluations to detect residual classes, choose cup primitives, and obtain necessary first-order lift matrices. Their span contains all required rectangular/square/alternating matrices; parity permits invertible alternating blocks. A full-rank first-order differential gives a nonzero initial term of an actual maximal minor, proving the stated residual determinant tests after finitely many added directions.

Read section 05: construct integral Siegel classes through a relative homology lattice with primitive period evaluation; calibrate exact dual-exponential coordinates. Line-switch comparisons prove integrality of a normalized coordinate only after separately removing smoothing and fixed Euler divisors. In rank one, a nonzero tame-height direction, cup comparison and exact spectral-height identity determine the central logarithmic coordinate. Integral Poitou-Tate and Haar factors cancel all omitted Euler factors and identify v_p(U(0))=X_p(E)>=0 for non-CM curves.

Read section 06: construct integral depleted logarithmic primitives on the ordinary modular source (without an ordinary-reduction assumption on E), bounded CM disk measures and exact character/central interpolation. Descend analytic principal ideals; prove vertical analytic primitivity via tame-stalk independence. At high characters, exact local Kummer lines and horizontal square switches preserve determinant valuations and give divisibility. Integral Weierstrass division upgrades this to U_w=B_w/L_w in R with p not dividing U_w; trace identities give exact removal of added tame variables. Horizontal quotient divisors still remain.

Roadmap only from read section 01; sections 07-10 unread: theta implications at nonaugmentation tests and growing p-level make quotient factors regular; character division identifies quotient ideals and added tame directions exclude simultaneous codimension-one jumps, making the quotients units. Integral specialization at the center yields the pair discrepancy identity; combine with the non-CM one-sided inequality and CM rank-zero input.
